title: Artin–Schreier pole tests over a complete DVR
statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic $p$, let $\pi$ be a uniformizer, and put $E=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-pc-field-extension]. For $a\in E$ put $H=E[T]/(T^p-T-a)$, and let $D$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $H$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. The following tests hold. (A) If $a\in R$, then $\mathfrak m_RD_q=qD_q$ for every maximal ideal $q$ of $D$, and the corresponding residue field extension is finite separable. (B) If $a=\pi^{-n}u$ with $u\in R^\times$, $n>0$ and $p\nmid n$, then $H$ is a field of degree $p$, $D$ is a complete DVR, $D/\mathfrak m_D=k$, and $\mathfrak m_RD=\mathfrak m_D^p$. (C) If $a=\pi^{-n}u$ with $u\in R^\times$, $n>0$, $p\mid n$, and $\bar u\notin k^p=\{c^p:c\in k\}$, then $H$ is a field of degree $p$, $D=R[\pi^{n/p}T]$ is a complete DVR, $\mathfrak m_RD=\mathfrak m_D$, and $D/\mathfrak m_D=k[\bar u^{1/p}]$ is purely inseparable of degree $p$ over $k$. Here $D_q$ denotes localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], finite means finitely generated as a module, and purely inseparable in the last clause means that the $p$th power of every element lies in $k$.

source.place: Tag 09F0, lemma-pre-characteristic-p-case, implications (A), (B), (C), specialized to complete DVRs; the statement records the explicit pole criteria, not a new general normalization theorem.

proof.text: For (A), set $B=R[T]/(T^p-T-a)$. The monic power basis makes $B$ finite free of rank $p$ and identifies $B[1/\pi]=H$. Its polynomial has derivative $-1$. In the derivative-inverse presentation the additional generator is therefore $Y=-1$; eliminating $Y$ identifies that presentation with $B$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is finite etale. A DVR is a PID, so the cited PID lemma makes $R$ normal and Noetherian. Apply the finite-etale normal-component theorem to $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$: its hypotheses of integrality, normality and Noetherianity now hold. It identifies $B$ with the product of the integral closures of $R$ in the field factors of $H$. Integrality in a finite product is coordinatewise: one implication projects a monic equation, and conversely the product of the finitely many monic equations annihilating the coordinates annihilates the tuple. Hence $B=D$.

Still in (A), every element of $D$ is integral over $R$ by its definition. The integral-contraction lemma shows that a maximal ideal $q$ of $D$ contracts to the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$. The morphism just constructed is etale, hence unramified and locally of finite type by the definition of etale. Apply the unramified local-ring criterion at $q$ and $\mathfrak m_R$. Since $R_{\mathfrak m_R}=R$, its conclusion is precisely $\mathfrak m_RD_q=qD_q$ and that $\kappa(q)/k$ is finite separable. This allows both the split and the field case of $H$; no irreducibility has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 09F0, lemma-pre-characteristic-p-case, Case (A); Tag 00U4, lemma-etale-at-prime; Tag 02GF, lemma-unramified-at-point

proof.text: For (B), the injective map $R\hookrightarrow E$ makes $E$ a field of characteristic $p$, and $H$ has its canonical coefficient $E$-algebra structure. Let $v$ be the normalized additive valuation of $R$, extended to $E^\times$ by fractions. There is no $b\in E$ with $b^p-b=a$: $b=0$ is excluded by $a\ne0$; for $b\ne0$, if $v(b)\geq0$ the left side is in $R$, whereas $v(a)=-n<0$; if $v(b)<0$, the two terms have distinct valuations $pv(b)<v(b)$ and therefore $v(b^p-b)=pv(b)$, which would give $p\mid n$. The valuation assertion follows directly by factoring out the smaller uniformizer power: the remaining sum is a unit plus an element of the maximal ideal, hence is a unit. The converse clause of [lem-sfb-epp-artin-schreier-presentation], applied to this characteristic-$p$ field and this quotient with its coefficient structure, excludes the product case and implies that $H$ is a normal separable field extension of $E$ of degree $p$. Complete-DVR normalization gives a finite complete DVR $D$ with fraction field $H$ and a local inclusion $R\hookrightarrow D$.

Write $z$ for the class of $T$ in $H$, and let $w$ be the normalized additive valuation of $D$. Put $e=w(\pi)>0$. Units of $R$ remain units of $D$, since their inverses remain in $D$, so $w(a)=-ne$. The equation forces $w(z)<0$; factoring out the smaller power as in the preceding step gives $pw(z)=-ne$. Since $p\nmid n$, this implies $p\mid e$. Apply the Galois degree-data lemma to the normal separable degree-$p$ extension $H/E$. The integral closure is the local ring $D$, so its number $g$ of maximal ideals is $1$, and the formula is $p=ef$ with $f=[D/\mathfrak m_D:k]\geq1$. Consequently $e=p$ and $f=1$. The induced residue-field map is therefore an isomorphism, and $\pi$ is a unit times a $p$th power of a uniformizer of $D$, giving $\mathfrak m_RD=\mathfrak m_D^p$. This proves every assertion of (B).

For (C), put $h=n/p\geq1$, $c=\pi^{n-h}$ and $F(Y)=Y^p-cY-u$. Then $n-h=(p-1)h>0$. Set $B=R[Y]/(F)$ and let $y$ be its generator. The monic quotient lemma makes $B$ free of rank $p$ and identifies $B/\pi B$ with $k[Y]/(Y^p-\bar u)$. The non-$p$th-power hypothesis and the cited irreducibility theorem make the latter a field of degree $p$; its basis is $1,\bar y,\ldots,\bar y^{p-1}$. The finite-free field-fibre criterion applies, so $B$ is a DVR, $R\hookrightarrow B$ is injective, and $\mathfrak m_B=\pi B$.

The substitutions $y\mapsto\pi^hT$ and $T\mapsto\pi^{-h}y$ define inverse maps $B[1/\pi]\cong H$: indeed $F(\pi^hT)=\pi^n(T^p-T-a)$. A DVR with uniformizer $\pi$ has fraction field $B[1/\pi]$, so $H$ is a field. Its dimension over $E$ is $p$ by the monic power basis. View $B$ as the subring $R[\pi^hT]$ of $H$. The inclusion $R\hookrightarrow B$ is local because $\mathfrak m_B=\pi B$ and $B/\pi B$ contains $k$ as a subfield. The uniqueness clause of complete-DVR normalization therefore identifies $B$ with $D$ and gives its completeness. Thus $\mathfrak m_RD=\mathfrak m_D$ and the residue field is $k[Y]/(Y^p-\bar u)=k[\bar u^{1/p}]$. Every element has a representative $\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}a_i\bar y^i$; its $p$th power is $\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}a_i^p\bar u^i\in k$. Together with the degree-$p$ basis this proves the purely inseparable assertion of (C).
